benefits.heading: More visibility and networking, with less manual effort
benefits.lead: The ORIF interface makes theatre programmes usable wherever they still have to be copied by hand today.

features.title: More efficient workflows
features.body: Implement once, benefit over time: programme data no longer has to be typed into different input masks. Automated transfer keeps information up to date without additional maintenance.

features.title: Greater reach
features.body: Machine-readable programmes can appear on many platforms with little extra effort. ORIF builds bridges between data silos and translates different formats into one shared standard.

features.title: A larger network
features.body: Smart Theatre Services lay the groundwork for connecting open and protected cultural data. The interface can also be used by a theatre immediately, even before using the data space.

network.heading: More than 140 institutions in the network
network.lead: Theatres, associations, platforms, archives and software partners from Germany, Austria and Switzerland are already working with machine-readable programmes.
network.statLabel: institutions are currently part of the network.
network.imageAlt: Map of Germany, Austria and Switzerland with coloured dots marking theatres, associations and platforms in the Smart Theatre Services network.

stakeholders.heading: Benefits for every stakeholder
stakeholders.lead: Whether theatre management, PR team, artistic administration or technical partners: everyone benefits from a shared standard.

features.title: Theatre management
features.body: With minimal technical effort, programmes become machine-readable. This increases visibility and positions the theatre as a pioneer of digital transformation.

features.title: PR and marketing
features.body: Programmes can be published automatically on multiple platforms and updated in real time. That means less manual work and stronger communications.

features.title: Artistic administration
features.body: Venue, rehearsal, production, ticket and touring planning all benefit when data can be connected seamlessly across systems.

features.title: Developers and agencies
features.body: Existing programme data only needs to be mapped once to the ORIF data model and can then become compatible with many applications.

pitch.heading: We lay the pipeline – you keep control
body: This project is commissioned by the Deutscher Bühnenverein as Use Case 3 of the Cultural Data Space and is part of Germany's digital strategy.
Theatres get a standardised interface for their programmes – and remain the owners of their data.

imageVideo.title: Smart Theatre Services – Project video

items.body: We no longer have to copy our programmes into five different forms. The interface really takes the pressure off our PR team.
We did not want to simply hand over our data. With ORIF we keep sovereignty – and decide ourselves what appears where.
An open standard built on Schema.org and the GND is exactly what archives and search systems have needed for years.
